India 2027

Five states elect new assemblies in early 2027. Pick a state on the map or from the list to open its seat map.

Built to be the one place to follow the 2027 state elections, from old results to the new ones. Right now that means the full 2022 result for every one of these 690 seats — winner, runner-up, vote shares and margins. As the 2027 election cycle moves from party declarations and Election Commission dates to counting day itself, Ginti will add live, seat-by-seat results and counting alongside election news and stories, in the same place.

About the data

What the site shows

Every seat map shows the 2022 assembly election result: who won each constituency, the runner-up, their vote shares and the margin. Nothing on the site is a forecast or a projection of 2027.

Seats are coloured by the alliance their winner fought with in 2022. Where a party has changed sides since then, a note under "Alliances in 2022" on the state's page says so.

The Election Commission events and Election news lists are compiled by hand from news reports, with a link to each source. They show the date they were last compiled and do not update on their own.

Data and limits

Constituency and state boundaries: DataMeet's community maps (CC BY 2.5 India). 2022 results: Uttar Pradesh from the open up-election-data set; Punjab, Uttarakhand, Goa and Manipur from Wikipedia's results-by-constituency tables. Seat totals for all five states match the official 2022 tallies. Individual vote shares were not checked against ECI Form 21 reports.

The MLA shown for each seat is the 2022 winner. By-elections and defections since 2022 are not reflected.

Polling dates are not announced. Assembly terms end on 13 March (Manipur), 14 March (Goa), 16 March (Punjab), 28 March (Uttarakhand) and 22 May 2027 (Uttar Pradesh).

References & sources

Ginti shows only the 2022 assembly election results. These are the official bodies and independent websites that publish Indian election and political data — use them to check what you see here, or to read further.

About this list Ginti is not affiliated with any site listed here. Descriptions are short summaries and each site may change over time. Check a site's own terms before reusing its data. Last reviewed 12 November 2026.

Official sources

Where election results and parliamentary information originate.

Official

Election Commission of India

eci.gov.in

The constitutional body that runs elections. Publishes statistical reports and final results for past elections, including constituency-wise detail.

Use for: the primary source for election results.

Official

PRS Legislative Research

prsindia.org

An independent, not-for-profit group that tracks and analyses Parliament and state legislatures, with a "Find Your MP" tool and bill tracking.

Reuse: licensed under Creative Commons Attribution 4.0.

Official

Digital Sansad

sansad.in

The Parliament of India's digital portal, built by the National Informatics Centre, for parliamentary records and member information.

Use for: parliamentary reference, not election results.

Candidates & representatives

Background, assets and performance of candidates and sitting members.

Independent

MyNeta

myneta.info

Run by the Association for Democratic Reforms (ADR). Shows candidates' declared criminal cases, assets and liabilities, education and income from election affidavits.

Note: self-declared and archived data — check the latest affidavit.

Independent

NetaWorth

netaworth.vercel.app

Makes the declared wealth of sitting MLAs and MPs searchable, with a state map, comparisons and wealth growth over time. Cites ECI, ADR and MyNeta. Open source.

Note: built on affidavit data — check the cited affidavit.

Independent

NetaScore100

netascore100.in

A data-driven transparency platform scoring Lok Sabha MPs using fund-utilisation data from MoSPI, attendance and debates from PRS, and candidate data from MyNeta.

Note: scores follow the site's own method — read how they are worked out.

Independent

Track My Neta

trackmyneta.com

Report cards for MPs and MLAs on local development, infrastructure, education and healthcare, based on citizen reviews and GPS-based area tracking.

Note: ratings come from citizen reviews, not official data.

Results & encyclopaedias

Historical results and general political reference.

Independent

IndiaVotes

indiavotes.com

A national database of Indian elections, political data and historical election results.

Use for: comparing past results across elections.

Independent

Netapedia

netapedia.in

An independent political encyclopaedia with interactive content and election insights.

Use for: background reading on politicians and elections.

Party declarations used on Ginti come from each party's own official announcements or Election Commission filings, with the source and date shown where they appear.
